Unity Introduction.exp: Introduction to Unity and its ecosystem.

Hello Unity:
Unity uses a component-based architecture. Game objects are empty containers that get behavior from attached components. Scripts are written in C# and inherit from MonoBehaviour. The Start() method runs once at initialization, and Update() runs every frame.

Create a C# script, attach it to a GameObject, and use Start() to print to the console. Press Play to see your output in the Console window.

Augmented Reality: AR Foundation provides a cross-platform AR framework for iOS (ARKit) and Android (ARCore). Key components: ARSession (manages AR lifecycle), ARPlaneManager (detects surfaces), ARPointCloudManager (feature points), ARAnchorManager (world anchors), and ARRaycastManager (hit testing). Place virtual objects on detected planes with ARPlacementInteractable.

Working with Components: Everything in Unity is a GameObject with components. Transform is the only required component (position, rotation, scale). You can add components like Rigidbody (physics), Collider (collision detection), Renderer (visuals), and custom scripts. Use GetComponent<T>() to access components at runtime.

Colliders & Rigidbodies: Unity's physics system uses Rigidbody components for physics-driven movement and Colliders for shape definition. Use Physics.Raycast() for line-of-sight and shooting. Colliders can be triggers (no physical response) for detection zones. Physics Materials control friction and bounciness. Joints connect Rigidbodies together (Hinge, Fixed, Spring, Configurable).

Prefab System: Prefabs are reusable GameObject templates. Create a GameObject, drag it to the Project window to make a prefab. Nested prefabs contain other prefabs. Prefab variants inherit from a base prefab with overrides. Use Instantiate() to spawn prefabs at runtime. The Prefab Mode allows editing the prefab in isolation without affecting scene instances.

Shader Graph: Shader Graph is Unity's node-based shader editor for creating shaders without code. Supports Universal RP and HDRP. PBR Graph (physically-based) vs Unlit Graph. Master Stack controls final output: Vertex, Fragment, Surface options. Use Sub Graphs for reusable node groups. Keywords enable multi-compile shader variants. Blackboard properties expose parameters to the inspector.

UXML & USS: UI Toolkit is Unity's web-inspired UI system. UXML defines layout structure (like HTML), USS provides styling (like CSS). Runtime UI for in-game HUD and menus, Editor UI for tool windows. Data binding connects UI elements to C# data sources. The UI Builder window enables visual editing. Event system supports propagation, pooling, and custom events.

<ui:UXML xmlns:ui="UnityEngine.UIElements">
  <ui:VisualElement class="hud-container">
    <ui:Label text="Score: 0" name="ScoreLabel" class="score-text" />
    <ui:ProgressBar name="HealthBar" low-value="0" high-value="100" value="100" />
    <ui:VisualElement class="inventory-row" name="InventoryRow">
      <ui:Button text="Item 1" class="inv-slot" />
      <ui:Button text="Item 2" class="inv-slot" />
      <ui:Button text="Item 3" class="inv-slot" />
    </ui:VisualElement>
    <ui:Button text="Pause" name="PauseButton" />
  </ui:VisualElement>
</ui:UXML>

// C# controller
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.UIElements;

public class HUDController : MonoBehaviour
{
    private UIDocument document;
    private Label scoreLabel;
    private ProgressBar healthBar;

    void OnEnable()
    {
        document = GetComponent<UIDocument>();
        var root = document.rootVisualElement;

        scoreLabel = root.Q<Label>("ScoreLabel");
        healthBar = root.Q<ProgressBar>("HealthBar");

        root.Q<Button>("PauseButton").clicked += () =>
        {
            Time.timeScale = Time.timeScale == 0 ? 1 : 0;
        };

        // Style manipulation
        scoreLabel.style.color = Color.yellow;
    }

    public void SetScore(int score) => scoreLabel.text = $"Score: {score}";
    public void SetHealth(float percent) => healthBar.value = percent;
}

Mecanim & Animator: Mecanim is Unity's animation system. The Animator Controller defines a state machine with states (idle, walk, run) and transitions. Blend Trees blend multiple animations by parameter (speed, direction). Avatar masks enable layered animation (upper body shooting while walking). Apply Root Motion for animation-driven movement. Animation Events trigger code at specific frames.

Data Architecture: ScriptableObjects are data containers that avoid MonoBehaviour overhead. Use them for game events, item definitions, dialogue trees, level configs, and audio settings. Create assets at runtime with CreateInstance(). Use [CreateAssetMenu] for easy asset creation. They enable data-driven architecture — designers can tweak values without touching code.

UGS: Unity Gaming Services is Unity's cloud platform providing Authentication, Cloud Save, Lobby, Relay (P2P), Economy, Analytics, and Cloud Code. Players can sign in anonymously or with external providers. Cloud Save persists player progress. Lobby + Relay enables multiplayer without custom backend. All services integrate through the Unity Gaming Services SDK.

Scene Management: Multi-scene workflows split a game into additive scenes: persistent managers, UI layer, gameplay levels. Use LoadSceneMode.Additive to load without unloading. SceneManager.sceneLoaded event tracks loading. DontDestroyOnLoad keeps objects across scenes. Addressables provide async scene loading with dependency management and remote content delivery.

Custom Editors: Unity Editor can be extended with Custom Editors (replace inspector UI), PropertyDrawers (custom field rendering), EditorWindows (standalone tool windows), Gizmos (in-scene visualization), and MenuItems. Use IMGUI or UI Toolkit for editor UI. SerializedObject and SerializedProperty provide safe data access with Undo support.

Navigation: Unity's AI Navigation system bakes a NavMesh from scene geometry. NavMeshAgent handles pathfinding and movement. OffMeshLinks connect disconnected areas (jumps, ladders). NavMeshObstacle dynamically affects the navmesh. The system uses RVO (Reciprocal Velocity Obstacles) for agent avoidance. Bake settings control agent radius, height, slope, and step offset.

Visual Effects: VFX Graph is Unity's GPU-accelerated particle system with node-based graph editing. Supports millions of particles with minimal CPU overhead. Use events to trigger particle bursts, exposed properties for runtime control, and custom blocks with Shader Graph integration. Capacities set maximum concurrent particles. Output updates: Lit Quad, Mesh, Line, Trail, Ribbon.

ECS & Burst Compiler: Unity's Data-Oriented Tech Stack (DOTS) includes Entities (archetypes), Components (struct data only), and Systems (logic). The Burst Compiler translates C# to highly optimized native code via LLVM. The Jobs System provides safe multithreading with dependency management. Together they enable processing thousands of entities at high performance with no GC allocations.

Sprites & 2D World: Unity's 2D features include SpriteRenderer for rendering sprites, SpriteShape for terrain/rails, and SpriteMask for visibility. Sorting Layers and Order in Layer control draw order. 2D physics uses Rigidbody2D, Collider2D variants (Box, Circle, Polygon, Edge), and PhysicsMaterial2D. CompositeCollider2D merges colliders on a single body.

AudioSources & Mixers: Unity's audio system uses AudioSource to play AudioClip assets. AudioMixer provides bus routing with groups (Master, Music, SFX, Voice) and effects (reverb, EQ, compression). Spatial Blend controls 2D vs 3D positioning. 3D audio uses distance attenuation curves and Doppler effect. AudioReverbZone creates realistic environment transitions.

Intelligent Cameras: Cinemachine provides modular camera system with virtual cameras. CinemachineVirtualCamera defines camera behavior: FramingTransposer (follow), FreeLook (3rd person orbit), BlendList (cutscene sequences). Priority system blends between cameras. Noise (Perlin) adds screen shake. Dolly tracks animate cameras along paths. Aim components: Composer, GroupComposer, HardLookAt.

Multi-Language Support: Unity's Localization package manages multiple languages via String Tables and Asset Tables. Use LocalizeStringEvent for UI text and LocalizeSpriteEvent for images. Locale selection at runtime via LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale. Smart Strings with placeholders ({0}, {count}) handle pluralization. Font fallback ensures CJK and special character support.

Terrain Engine: Unity's Terrain system creates large outdoor environments. Paint heightmaps, textures (albedo, normal), trees, and details (grass, bushes). Terrain layers blend textures based on height and angle. Wind Zones animate vegetation. Tree Creator generates procedural trees. Use Terrain Settings for pixel error, base map distance, and detail object density.

Unity Data.exp: Working with data and APIs in Unity.

Lighting & Probes: Unity lighting includes Directional (sun), Point (bulb), Spot (cone), and Area (rectangle) lights. Real-time vs baked lighting. Lightmapping: bake indirect lighting into lightmaps with Progressive Lightmapper. Reflection Probes capture environment reflections on metallic/glossy surfaces. Light Probe Groups provide indirect lighting on dynamic objects. Emission on materials contributes to baked lighting.

Performance & Pooling: Object pooling prevents GC spikes by reusing objects instead of instantiate/destroy. The Profiler window shows CPU/GPU/Rendering/Memory usage. Frame Debugger: Window > Analysis > Frame Debugger to inspect draw calls. Key optimizations: reduce draw calls (static batching, GPU instancing), LOD groups, occlusion culling, texture atlasing, and reducing material count.
